key_insight: Clustering brain elements by their strain histories enables over 200:1 compression while retaining high-fidelity representations of simulated brain strain.
engineering_relevance: Compact strain representations reduce storage burdens and support downstream analysis and machine learning for traumatic brain injury biomechanics.
method: Extract features from element-wise maximum principal strain (MPS) time histories.
Apply K-means to build clustering templates with 8–8192 clusters.
Evaluate reconstruction fidelity against the original finite element strain data.
evidence_signal: Using 3,693 THUMS impact simulations with 118,840 brain elements, K = 512 achieved over 200:1 compression with mean element-wise peak MPS RMSE of 0.027; K = 4096 achieved 30:1 compression with RMSE of 0.016.
watch_item: Transferability to other head models or impact conditions is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Clustering Templates: A Data-Driven Framework for Dimensionality Reduction and Compression of Brain Strain in Head Impact
